name: Pearl Continental Hotel Bhurban
assumptions: Storey height 3.3 m is assumed; six storeys come from a booking site and match the valley side in the photos.
No published height: floors plus the roof fitted to the photos give the eaves at 12.5 m and the main ridge at 20 m above the footprint ground.
The lowest terrace floor is placed 4 m below the footprint ground: the hillside falls to the east but its exact profile under the building is unknown (coarse elevation model only).
Terrace reach of 3.5, 7 and 10.5 m beyond the wall is read from the satellite tile at about 0.5 m per pixel and the photos; the real tiers vary from wing to wing.
Roof colour is a pale metal grey from daylight photos and the satellite; the blue in one dusk photo is treated as light, not paint.
Road (west) side: no photo found. Its massing follows the footprint and the satellite; the window rows there and on the rear block are plain guesses.
Rear block E: only its roof is visible in the sources, so its walls are plain.
No main entrance or porch is modelled because no source shows it.
Wing C upper roof height 23 m is estimated from the aerial photo; the skirt roof, short wall and skylight are simplified.
Corner towers and stair cores are placed from photos; their plan sizes are estimated.
